summary: Del Norte County lookout point; a 1923 record describes a guard's broken phone and a mile-long walk to report fires. No build date or present state found.

staffing.status: guard at the lookout point (1923 record)

events.note: The 1923 entry refers to a guard working at the lookout point, with the guard's camp a mile away. It is not a staffing schedule.

evidence.supports: Listing places Lookout Point in Del Norte County under Six Rivers National Forest
evidence.quote: Del Norte County - Six Rivers National Forest

evidence.supports: Entry is quoted from the Chronological History of the Klamath National Forest, Vol. III, 1921-1930
evidence.quote: (Chronological History of the Klamath National Forest, Vol. III, 1921-1930)

evidence.supports: Entry asks for a standard telephone line between the guard's camp and the lookout point, one mile away; the emergency wire is not holding up
evidence.quote: There is a need for a standard telephone line between the Guard's camp and the Lookout point one mile away. The emergency wire is not holding up.

evidence.supports: No shelter at the lookout point; iron phone not working so the guard hiked a mile to report a fire
evidence.quote: There is no shelter at the Lookout point. The iron phone at the Lookout point is not working so the Guard has to hike a mile down to his camp to report a fire.

notes_for_editor: One source, a single 1923 entry quoted by the Forest Lookouts page. No build date, later use, fate or present state found. The firelookout.org California directory (https://firelookout.org/?p=1656) lists no Lookout Point in Del Norte County; its only Lookout Point is in Tulare County (Obs Pt, abandoned, 36.42932 -118.76237), which is a different site. The brief's coordinates (41.41512, -123.8079) have no source in this record. A web search found only Lookout Points in Washington State and the Bear Basin Butte / Camp Six lookout, which is a separate Six Rivers site and was not used. The 1923 entry comes from Klamath National Forest history; that the current manager is Six Rivers is taken from the brief and the listing, not verified separately.
